<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5defbfeb91829bb7885104a09ba114382aeab038`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5defbfeb91829bb7885104a09ba114382aeab038` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6cd2f201bf435c88b71b3c37870f053d507a9151` — the merge of head `5cb8ea25f1bd9c5df29083be6d667503c47c1da8` into base `5defbfeb91829bb7885104a09ba114382aeab038`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6cd2f201bf435c88b71b3c37870f053d507a9151 && git checkout 6cd2f201bf435c88b71b3c37870f053d507a9151
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5defbfeb91829bb7885104a09ba114382aeab038 5cb8ea25f1bd9c5df29083be6d667503c47c1da8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5defbfeb91829bb7885104a09ba114382aeab038 && git merge --no-ff 5cb8ea25f1bd9c5df29083be6d667503c47c1da8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5defbfeb91829bb7885104a09ba114382aeab038
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5defbfeb91829bb7885104a09ba114382aeab038` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The net diff is this card's.** Right. Against `main` `2f80f289` the head differs in five paths (the four the body names and the docs page); every other path equals main's blob. The body's `--remerge-diff` listing was not reproduced (the local clone is shallow); the net diff is the stronger reading.
- **Only the refusal arm moves.** Right. The admission rule is called from one place, the `catch` around the by-name read, and only when the thrown error is a package-scoped refusal (by class or by shape). A failed read, the missing caller resolution (`503`) and every resolved name leave that `catch` as they entered it. On main the same refusal answered `409`, so no request that ran before is refused now.
- **Admitted to none: `404`, byte-equal to a missing name.** Right. Both answers come from one function (`datasetNotFoundAnswer`). Pinned on the bare read, the caller arm, `?package=` naming a non-holder and the batch door.
- **An ambiguity with exactly one admitted holder runs that holder.** Right, and it runs the item read at that holder's exact address, so its bound overlay is the one judged and run. Pinned in both registration orders. With three holders and one admitted the door also runs it (measured: `200`).
- **Otherwise `409` naming only the admitted holders; `outside-closure` and `not-held-by-qualifier` never run anything.** Right. Pinned for two of three on the bare read and on the caller arm, and for both non-ambiguity reasons.
- **Undetermined admission: `503`, nothing run, no holder named.** Right. For an ambiguity the rule is `query_dataset`'s (an unjudged holder with fewer than two admitted). For the two non-ambiguity reasons it is `503` only when none is admitted, which is right because nothing is ever picked there. Measured: three holders, one unjudged, two admitted answer `409` naming the two; one unjudged and one admitted answer `503`; `?package=` naming a non-holder with one unjudged and one admitted answers `409` naming the admitted one.
- **Not moved: a resolved name keeps its answer (Q1, Q2).** Right. Four controls pin it, two of them on the `403` envelope.
- **Not moved: a service that is not plugin-wired is not asked.** Right as pinned: the control holds.
- **Not moved: a refusal naming the environment or the platform.** Right. The registry answers no environment item for a name a package holds, and no dataset source supplies a platform item, so such a candidate never sits beside a package holder. Measured on a name the environment holds: `?package=` naming a non-holder and the caller arm answer the same `409` naming the environment on main and here.
- **The batch door moves the same way.** Right, pinned.
- **`ambiguous-in-namespace`.** Listed in the rule and the table; see N3.
- **The PR's ablation table.** One independent leg was run here on a different line (the verdict itself, not the arm's entry). It reds the same eight pins as A0 and no control.
- One derived claim is judged under B1, not here.
- **Limb 2 census.** The three doors are where the body says and behave as it says: `savedHoldersOf` (dataset-tools.ts, line 267), `listSkillPrompts` and the face lookup (skill-prompts.ts, about lines 164 and 242), `readAgentRoster` (mcp-server-runtime.ts, line 1131), which lists every row and picks none. See N4 for one word. No code change is right for a limb the seat withdrew.

**Is every moved answer a widening?** FROM is `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` in every row.

| TO | Reading |
|:--|:--|
| `404 NOT_FOUND` | One refusal to another. The accept set does not move; ADR-0149 D2 asks for one answer for hidden and missing. Not a narrowing |
| `200` | The widening |
| `409` naming fewer holders | Status and `code` unchanged; the sentence names fewer. Not a narrowing |
| `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | One refusal to another, fail closed, nothing run. Not a narrowing |

No status narrows, so the narrowing carriers (`!`, a BREAKING paragraph, an ADR-0087 marker, a `Skills-docs:` line, the full dogfood battery) are not owed.

**Silent pick (ADR-0150 red line 2).** None found. The door runs a holder under a refusal only when the reason is an ambiguity, exactly one holder is admitted and none is unjudged. S1 names one composition for the epic seat to read.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/rest: patch`, title without `!`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` at the start of a line in both the PR body and the changeset. Right on all four: the change is a non-protocol widening, and nothing a metadata author writes moves.

Size: +549 / −45 over 5 files, under 3,000. No governed surface and no `packages/spec` path in the file list. The docs page is a prose face.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no other login to name.
- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report.
- `security_findings: none` in the dev report. B1 is the red-line read 6834745545's must-fix, handed to the card thread.
- The tier token. `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` reads this PR's face as the declaration face (no schema, no governed path, no narrowing; the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line decides), which maps to `TIER_DEFAULT`, exact and never a floor; this record carries that token.
- Deviation: the docs commit is outside the file surface claim 6817615501 declares, and the card carries no amendment at this read. Not judged here.
- The PR body predates the docs commit: it says four files, 65 commands for four paths, and "All readings are on head `890be0cd1`". It needs a refresh at the fix head.
- Deviation, branch name: harness-pinned, declared in the claim.
- Eight check-runs were still running at the read. The PR is a draft.

### ④ Design judgment

Against the card's Do 1 and ruling 6817809380: the order is the one asked (admission before the answer, on the refusal arm only), each candidate is read at its exact address so admission is judged on the item that would run, and the four outcomes are the four the ruling lists. The rule sits in one module with no analytics import, and the door calls it from one place. That design holds. The remainder is B1.

**B1 — must-fix. Target: card #32292, the fix head.** The red-line read 6834745545's must-fix, handed to the card thread with its repro; confirmed here by measurement, on this source and on main's blob. A delta round is owed on the fix head.

**S1 — should-fix, with the fix head (else a new card under #31527). A holder whose saved definition fails the dataset parse counts as admitted to none, and neither the body nor the changeset says so.**

Measured, two packages holding `sales`, one definition malformed:

| Request | main | This head |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Bare name, caller with read access to the valid holder's object (or to both objects) | `409` naming both | `200`, the valid holder runs |
| Bare name, caller with read access to neither | `409` naming both | `404` |
| `?package=` naming the malformed holder | `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` | `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` |

This is `query_dataset`'s rule ("an item the parse left out is refused for every caller, so it is admitted to none"), and the module's jsdoc states it. Two things are missing. The moved-answers table and the changeset speak of "a caller admitted to fewer holders" without saying a malformed holder is one nobody is admitted to. And no pin holds it; the sibling branch, a holder whose exact address serves nothing (counted as unjudged), has no pin either. It is also the one composition where a caller with read access to both holders' objects gets one of them run, so the epic seat should read it by name.

Fix: one clause in the table and the changeset, and one pin for each of the two branches.

**N1 — nit, docs prose, with the fix head.** The paragraph `948903b5` adds agrees with the code except for two phrases. "Where two holders were in contention and exactly one is left" should read "two or more" (three holders with one admitted run it). "A holder whose dataset the caller may not query is never named" is true only where the analytics service is the one `AnalyticsServicePlugin` registers, as the changeset says. The other sentences match: `404` as for a missing name, `409` naming only the holders left, `503` when a verdict is missing and could change the answer, and the `403` of a resolved name.

**N2 — nit, prose in code, with the fix head.** The comment inside `readOne` (analytics-routes.ts) still says the resolver's refusal is "a declared `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming every candidate, which the catch below answers through its ADR-0112 arm". The admission arm now judges it first.

**N3 — nit, no card.** `ambiguous-in-namespace` is in the rule's ambiguity set and in the table, but this door takes no namespace address (`?package=` is an exact package id), so the reason cannot arrive here. Harmless.

**N4 — nit, PR body, no card.** The census says both doors "take the first row". `savedHoldersOf` takes a holder's first row that parsed, else its first row. The reach claim (one row per package on the merged list, no package dataset rows on the stdio fallback) was read, not re-measured.

Sentence-by-sentence agreement otherwise: the module's jsdoc, the `[#32292]` comments in the door, the changeset's four moved answers and its "Unchanged" paragraph match the code, apart from what B1 and S1 cover.

Delta review owed on the fix head: B1's fix, S1, and the docs paragraph if its sentences move.

Neither is reviewed here; this record stands on `948903b5` only, and the delta round reads those two commits.
